note: `erasing` makes the same setup (it fixes the family with vanishing Ward sums, `silence`, and the weight-four rise); there is no bilinear form b_x, and the Kelvin/Wick content appears only as the commutation statement of `low_motion`.

theorem erasing (h : G.Simple) : erases (hierarchy F).spin (scheme F) := by
  refine ⟨4,?_⟩
  intro d hd T H W
  let P u v := brand F (d:=d) (T u v)
  let R := (scheme F).rise hd
  have hw u v : silence G d (P u v) := (branded F _).mp (fun n w x hx => W n x hx u v w)
  have ht (u v) (p : (Model F).Field 4) : T u v (R p)∈LinearMap.range R := H.rises _ hd u v p

proof_context.conclusion: `erasing` fixes the family `T u v` (the map Δ) with all Ward sums vanishing and turns that into `hw`, the branded `T u v` being `silence`, with `R` the weight-four rise.

lemma low_motion (h : G.Simple) {d} (hd : 4≤d) {T : Module.End ℂ (WickPol G)} (H : silence G d T)
    (ht : ∀ p ∈ shellSector G 4,T p∈shellSector G 4)
    (a : Axis) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {v : E4} (hv : ‖v‖=r) {p : WickPol G} (hp : p∈shellSector G 4) :
    let x := (-r) • basis a
    reflectPol (house x * house v) (T p) = T (reflectPol (house x * house v) p) := by

proof_context.conclusion: A silent `T` preserving the weight-four shell sector commutes with `reflectPol (house x * house v)` on that sector; this is the Kelvin/Wick two-point content.
